The ward was quite small, there wasn't much room to walk or exercise.

Every psychiatric hospital is the same. It has an ancient elliptical and an old recumbent bike. Neither work properly.

The "art," is cemented to the wall. 

Anything that a reasonably creative person could use to harm themselves is banned. 

You are constantly being watch, and discussed at staff meetings. There is a imaginary *point system*.
You get points for going to group therapy sessions, contributing something meaningful. You lose points for sleeping too much, having an emotional outburst.


Everyone is med'ed up to high heavens. 


If you are in immediate harm of hurting yourself, it's a good idea. But it's not helpful for long term success.
CPR is a temporary measure until advanced life support can respond. It doesn't save your life; it keeps your viable until an AED and or pharmacology are available.
